problems.title: Multiply logarithms with related bases
problems.question: Evaluate log₅7·log₄₉125.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Change of base: logₐb=ln b/ln a.
steps: The product is (ln7/ln5)(3ln5/(2ln7))=3/2.

problems.title: A logarithm of a reciprocal
problems.question: Evaluate log base (7+4√3) of (7−4√3).
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
steps: The argument is the reciprocal of the positive base, and that base is not 1. Its logarithm is −1.

problems.title: A constant logarithmic function with a restricted input
problems.question: Which quadrant contains the graph of f(x)=log base x⁹ of x²?
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Logarithm base requires x⁹>0,x⁹≠1; change of base gives 2ln x/(9ln x).
steps: The domain is x>0,x≠1. On this domain f(x)=2/9>0.
Both coordinates are positive, so the graph is in quadrant I.

problems.title: Apothem of a regular triangular pyramid
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has base side 6 and height 7. Find its apothem.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Equilateral-base inradius=s√3/6; apothem²=height²+inradius².
steps: The base inradius is √3. The apothem is √(49+3)=√52.

problems.title: An oblique prism’s perpendicular section
problems.question: An oblique prism has volume 72 and lateral edge 4. Find its normal-section area.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Volume=normal-section area×lateral edge.
steps: The requested area is 72/4=18.

problems.title: Combine logarithms after a positive-domain check
problems.question: Solve log₁₉x+log₁₉(x²)=3.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Domain x>0; logarithm sum=log₁₉(x³).
steps: x³=19³, so the unique allowed root is x=19.

problems.title: A sum of reciprocal logarithms
problems.question: Evaluate $\sum_{b\in\{\sqrt2,\sqrt4,\sqrt8,\sqrt{16}\}}1/\log_b(\sin(\pi/4))$.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: 1/log_b t=log_t b and sin(π/4)=2⁻¹/².
steps: The four bases are 2¹/²,2¹,2³/²,2². Their logarithms to base 2⁻¹/² are −1,−2,−3,−4.
The sum is −10.

problems.title: Opposite signs force both sides to zero
problems.question: Solve log₂(cos²x)=sin⁸x.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Where defined, 0<cos²x≤1, so the logarithm is nonpositive; sin⁸x is nonnegative.
steps: Equality requires both sides zero. cos²x=1 and sin x=0 occur exactly at x=kπ, and these are in the domain.

problems.title: Digit count of a large power
problems.question: Given log₁₀3=0.4771…, how many decimal digits does 3¹⁰⁰ have?
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Digits of positive integer N=floor(log₁₀N)+1.
steps: log₁₀(3¹⁰⁰)=47.71…, so its floor is 47. The digit count is 48.

problems.title: Volume from a right parallelepiped’s shorter diagonal
problems.question: A right parallelepiped has base sides 2,6, acute angle 60°, and shorter space diagonal √31. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Shorter base diagonal squared=2²+6²−2×2×6cos60°=28.
steps: Height squared=31−28=3. Base area=2×6sin60°=6√3.

problems.title: Equal exponential terms by change of base
problems.question: Solve $x^{\log_37}+7^{\log_3x}=14$.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Domain x>0; identity $x^{\log_a b}=b^{\log_a x}$.
steps: The two terms are equal, so 7^(log₃x)=7. Since the base 7 is injective, log₃x=1 and x=3.

problems.title: A logarithm of a product
problems.question: log₂3=a, log₂5=b. Express log₄15.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: log₄15=log₂(3×5)/log₂4.
steps: The numerator is a+b and denominator 2.

problems.title: An inequality characterizing an increasing function
problems.question: f(x)=3ˣ. Which listed inequality holds for every real x,y?
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: A strictly increasing function has the same order in inputs and outputs.
steps: x−y and f(x)−f(y) always have the same sign, or are both zero. Their product is therefore nonnegative.

problems.title: Axial area of a cone frustum
problems.question: A cone frustum has radii 12,7 cm and generator inclination 45° to a base. Find axial-section area.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Height=(R−r)tan45°; the axial section has parallel sides 2R,2r.
steps: Height=5. The trapezoid area is (24+14)×5/2=95 cm².

problems.title: Circumsphere of a square-pyramid frustum
problems.question: A regular square frustum has base sides 7,1 cm and lateral-edge inclination 45°. Find its circumsphere radius.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Edge horizontal displacement=3√2, so height=3√2; circumcentre lies on the symmetry axis.
steps: Put the lower base at z=0 and upper at z=3√2. Their squared circumradii are 49/2 and 1/2.
If the sphere centre is at z=t, equal vertex distances give 49/2+t²=1/2+(3√2−t)². Thus t=−1/√2.
The sphere radius squared is 49/2+1/2=25, so radius 5 cm.

problems.title: A reciprocal logarithm system
problems.question: Solve logᵧx+logₓy=2, x²−y=20.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Both x,y>0 and neither equals 1; if t=logᵧx, then logₓy=1/t.
steps: t+1/t=2 gives (t−1)²=0, so t=1 and x=y.
x²−x−20=(x−5)(x+4)=0. Only x=y=5 meets the logarithm domain.

problems.title: Matching an upper bound with a lower bound
problems.question: Count roots of log₂(7+2x−x²)=4+x⁴−2x².
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: 7+2x−x²=8−(x−1)²≤8; right side=3+(x²−1)²≥3.
steps: The left side is at most 3, with equality only at x=1. The right side is at least 3.
At x=1 both equal 3 and the argument is positive. No other root can exist.

problems.title: A negative parabola and a positive exponential
problems.question: Count intersections of f(x)=−2x²+x−1 and g(x)=6⁻ˣ.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
steps: The two value signs are incompatible at every real input.

problems.title: A triangle spanning two prism levels
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has base side 8 cm and height 4 cm. Find area AB₁C.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Use AC as base. The distance from B₁ to AC combines the equilateral altitude and prism height perpendicularly.
steps: The equilateral altitude is 4√3. Thus B₁’s distance to AC is √(48+16)=8.
Area=8×8/2=32 cm².

problems.title: An off-axis section of a cylinder
problems.question: A cylinder’s axial section is a square of area 16 cm². Find the area of an axis-parallel section distance 1 from the axis.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Axial side=4 gives height 4,radius 2. Offset chord length=2√(r²−d²).
steps: The chord length is 2√3. Multiplying by height 4 gives 8√3 cm².

problems.title: A square written as two powers of two
problems.question: Natural m,k,n satisfy 2ᵐ+4ᵏ=n² and m>2k. Which listed m+k is possible?
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Divide by 2²ᵏ: the remaining square has form t²=2^(m−2k)+1.
steps: t is odd. The powers of two t−1,t+1 differ by 2, so they must be 2 and 4. Thus t=3 and m−2k=3.
Hence m+k=3k+3, a multiple of 3 at least 6. Among the listed values only 12 qualifies, attained at k=3,m=9,n=24.

problems.title: A logarithm of a piecewise rational argument
problems.question: Find the domain of log₃[(x+9)/(|x|−3)].
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: The whole argument must be strictly positive.
steps: For |x|>3 the denominator is positive, requiring x>−9. This gives (−9,−3) and (3,∞).
For −3<x<3 the denominator is negative but numerator positive, so no inputs qualify. All zero endpoints and poles are excluded.

problems.title: A logarithm substitution in a radical equation
problems.question: Solve $[(\log_2x)^3]/\sqrt{18-(\log_2x)^2}+(\log_2x)^2-18=0$.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Put t=log₂x, with x>0 and |t|<√18.
steps: The equation becomes t³=(18−t²)³/². Its right side is positive, so t>0. Taking cube roots gives t=√(18−t²).
Thus t²=9 and t=3, giving x=8. The negative t=−3 fails the unsquared equation.

problems.title: An insphere-to-base area ratio in a cone
problems.question: A sphere is inscribed in a cone. Sphere-surface/base-disk area=4:3. Find the cosine of the generator’s base inclination.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: With sphere radius r,cone base R,slant l,height h: r=Rh/(R+l); cos theta=R/l.
steps: 4πr²/(πR²)=4/3 gives r/R=1/√3. Put c=R/l. Then (r/R)²=h²/(R+l)²=(1−c)/(1+c).

problems.title: A sphere tangent to lateral faces on the base edges
problems.question: A triangular pyramid has base sides 7,8,9 and height 5. A sphere touches all lateral faces at points on the base edges. Find its radius.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Base inradius ρ=S/s. Such contact forces the apex and sphere centre onto the line normal to the base through its incenter.
steps: Heron gives s=12 and S=12√5, so ρ=√5. Let the sphere centre be signed height z above the base and apex height H=5.
At each contact T the sphere radius is perpendicular to the lateral face, hence to the segment from T to the apex. The normal-plane dot product gives ρ²+zH=0, so z=−ρ²/H=−1.
The sphere radius is √(ρ²+z²)=√6. The normal-line assertion follows because these perpendicularity equations give the apex projection equal signed distance to all three base sides.
